body_fields.quote:
The accessibility tree is built from the document on InitialTreeRequested and refreshed on change: on a poll that
reported work the shell's `View::poll` takes the document's changed set (`BaseDocument::take_changed_nodes` — outside
the `accessibility` cfg, so a shell built without the feature still drains it) and, under `accessibility`, rebuilds
the platform tree when the set it took was non-empty; both paths go through the `Document::accessibility_tree` trait
method, so a wrapper's override (DioxusDocument's stable ids) reaches the platform tree

a poll that takes a non-empty changed set rebuilds the platform tree, both paths through the
`Document::accessibility_tree` trait method, so a wrapper's override (DioxusDocument's stable ids) reaches it; proven
headlessly on the stand in both layout modes, its windowed witness at the platform adapter owed

body_fields.why: link (4) uses the changed set as its witness, so the probe must drain the set before the step it reads, and must not count node creation, hover or layout as state reaching a node.
body_fields.quote:
A harness settle (`Harness::settle`, the driver session's `act`) neither reads nor drains the set, so a step
settled through it leaves the refresh above, and a later diff, exactly what the step marked; and the set is non-empty
on a freshly booted harness document — the boot's own in-document mutations mark it and nothing has drained it — so a
check that reads `has_changes()` as "this step changed something" drains first

`changed_nodes` is the engine's changed set, the nodes written since the last `take_changed_nodes`: an
in-document mutation, a focus or checked change, a text control's input, a select's changed choice and a single
select's list opening or closing mark it — a page scroll or a move that closes a list marks its select through
`reconcile_select_list` at the next resolve, a wheel elsewhere through `close_select_list`; node creation, hover,
active, scroll and layout do not, save that scroll or move, and a highlight or a wheel move inside a list marks
nothing, so a pointer move alone reaches no refresh

body:
Builds a probe, in test or example code only, of the UI graph's four links (node to component, node to handlers, handler to state, state to reading nodes) as Dioxus 0.7.3 and escher's bridge dioxus-native-dom expose them with no fork-level change, each link given one of three verdicts.
Each verdict rests on a headless run on the seven_guis stand: a lean task where a handler writes state another node reads (Counter or CRUD) beside one served task, in both layout modes where layout touches the reading.
Link (2)'s answer for click says whether a node's click listener is readable from the listener map today (the deferred "reacts to a click" reading).
Re-verifies at HEAD the MountedData hazard's mechanism and coordinates (a task spawned from a key handler first polled inside render_immediate, panicking at events.rs:162) and names it in a plain-words reading for the founder, its fix brought as his fork with options, not decided or built.
Changes no Dioxus crate, no engine path for every document, and adds no verb, field, listener, log line or span; the UI graph itself is not built.

body_fields.what: the poll lines where a spawned task is first polled inside render_immediate while the document's RefCell is held
the MountedData call's RefCell already borrowed panic at events.rs:162
§A hazard measured beside step 15, the headless poll(None) measurement of the MountedData panic

body: The bridge's DioxusDocument element-id and listener reads, the surface every link of the probe reads through: in a Dioxus document every element node carries its stable element id as AccessKit author_id, and the probe addresses a node by that id rather than a new key.

The actionable-key rule and its check DioxusDocument::unkeyed_actionable, which already reads whether an element carries an event listener; link (2)'s click answer is the reading that rule's residual line owns (no snapshot field says an element reacts to a click), and the probe answers it without adding that field.

The snapshot model reads role, name and focus only off accessibility_tree, never a second role or name mapping; any role or name the probe reads of a node comes from the tree or the shared module's tables, and the probe adds no snapshot field, part or diff key.

The engine's changed set (changed_nodes, take_changed_nodes, has_changes) as a witness for link (4), state to the nodes that read it: a harness settle neither reads nor drains it and a fresh harness document's set is non-empty, so a probe reading it as this step changed something drains first; node creation, hover and layout do not mark it.

The accessibility tree's refresh on a poll that takes a non-empty changed set, through Document::accessibility_tree and DioxusDocument's override: the same poll path where the MountedData task is first polled inside render_immediate, re-verified headlessly and read, not run, on the windowed shell.

The keyboard harness press and press_with on the stand, through which a key handler is reached headlessly to drive the hazard's path (a key handler spawning a task that writes a signal), and the stand_keyboard and stand_snapshot_state checks that already drive keys through them.

Enter and Space dispatch of a Click to the focused button or control, where the app's handlers run before handle_click: the handler path whose written state links (3) and (4) read on the Counter or CRUD task.

The CRUD list as a stand surface for the handler-to-state links: crud-list, named People, a listbox whose option rows carry aria-selected and whose selection a row's click or the list's arrow keys write.

Values masked, never logged: nothing the probe reads (a component name, a handler, a signal's value) is printed, logged or put in a field; escher's log allowlist that redacts text, value, html and attrs for escher_* targets and the password MASKED_VALUE rule stay as they are, the probe adding no target, field or span.

The accessibility feature reaching seven_guis through escher-driver and no stand binary building a platform adapter: the probe stays headless, so the windowed path and any assistive-technology reading are read, not run, unless a reading needs them.
Both layout modes, the a11y plan's proof pattern for every stand reading: each verdict whose reading layout touches is measured in both.

body_fields.convention: a new stand check is asserted headlessly in both layout modes

body: Color contrast: Harness::text_contrast, contrast_ratio, stand_contrast's control, text and state tables and the visual lint's contrast reading; the probe reads no colour pair.
The single and multiple select's list behaviour: typeahead, the open list's keys and clicks, SelectListView colours, select_popup and stand_act_popup; the probe reads no select list.
The range input's keys, pointer value setting and step sanitizing.
Role derivation from the role attribute and the HTML-AAM element mapping, and the landmark roles inventory; the probe names no role.
The builder's ARIA name and description reads (aria-labelledby, aria-describedby, aria-description, label for) and the accessibility_label and accessibility_description checks.
Focusability, the inert focus fixup, disabled-ness keyed on the disabled attribute's presence, and the inert_subtree check.
Hidden content and visibility exclusion from the tree (aria-hidden, hidden, display none, visibility hidden) and hit-testing through inert.
The bridge's falsy-value removal of its 28 boolean attributes; the probe writes no attribute path.
The AccessKit platform adapter's creation before the window is shown and its windowed assistive-technology witness owned by a residuals line; no adapter is built.
Cells' grid keyboard model and its focus outline, and the load page's Tab order.
Cognitive cues: the flight booker's invalid dates and aria-invalid.
Motion, focus ring, colour scheme and user-preference tokens.
The not-yet-measured a11y violation schema, screen-reader test specs, live regions and skip links; the probe defines none of them.

body_fields.quote: The accessibility tree is built from the document on InitialTreeRequested and refreshed on change: on a poll that reported work the shell's `View::poll` takes the document's changed set (`BaseDocument::take_changed_nodes` — outside the `accessibility` cfg, so a shell built without the feature still drains it) and, under `accessibility`, rebuilds the platform tree when the set it took was non-empty; both paths go through the `Document::accessibility_tree` trait method, so a wrapper's override (DioxusDocument's stable ids) reaches the platform tree
The refresh on change is ratified by the founder (2026-10-07) — one item with the engine's changed-set contract in the next bullet.

body_fields.quote: `changed_nodes` is the engine's changed set, the nodes written since the last `take_changed_nodes`: a mutation of an in-document node, a focus or checked change, a text control's input, a select's changed choice and a single select's list opening or closing mark it
node creation, hover, active, scroll and layout do not, with no list open

A harness settle (`Harness::settle`, the driver session's `act`) neither reads nor drains the set, so a step settled through it leaves the refresh above, and a later diff, exactly what the step marked; and the set is non-empty on a freshly booted harness document — the boot's own in-document mutations mark it and nothing has drained it — so a check that reads `has_changes()` as "this step changed something" drains first

body_fields.quote: dioxus-native-dom's feature also gates its own `accessibility_tree` override, its snapshot model (`DioxusDocument::snapshot`), that model's text form (`Snapshot::to_text`) and its parts (`Snapshot::text_parts`), its diff (`Snapshot::diff`) and its actionable-key check (`DioxusDocument::unkeyed_actionable`), all five of which its crate doc names, and dioxus-native forwards the feature to blitz and to dioxus-native-dom

- a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support (sr-actionable-keys) requires that no snapshot field say an element reacts to a click. A `.andromeda/residuals.md` line (target: next) owns that reading, and the stand's count of elements that react to input but state no role is its starting reading. Link (2)'s `click` verdict feeds that residual and adds no field (`NODE_FIELDS` stays thirteen).
- a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support (sr-author-id) requires every element node of a Dioxus document to carry its stable element id as the AccessKit `author_id`, and the roles and names to be stated once. Any node → component reading must go through that id and leave it unchanged. It must add no second role or name mapping.
- a11y-plan §2 A11y Strategy (accessibility tree lifecycle) requires the tree to be built and refreshed through the `Document::accessibility_tree` trait method, so that DioxusDocument's stable-id override reaches it. A probe hook in `packages/dioxus-native-dom/` must not bypass that override.
- a11y-plan §2 A11y Strategy (`changed_nodes`) says a harness settle neither reads nor drains the changed set, and a fresh harness document's set is non-empty. So if a state → nodes reading leans on `has_changes()` or `take_changed_nodes`, it must drain first. A pointer move, hover or layout marks nothing.
- a11y-plan §5 Keyboard Navigation (keyboard-framework) records the MountedData hazard: a task spawned from a key handler that writes a signal panics at `events.rs:162`. For that reason Cells calls its handles synchronously. The probe must keep Cells' synchronous `MountedData::scroll_to` on arrow moves, and any fix stays the founder's fork. Whether HEAD still has this mechanism and these coordinates after the 2026-11-01 sync is research's question.
- a11y-plan §5 Keyboard Navigation (per-surface keyboard shortcuts) requires Cells' `cells-grid` to be one Tab stop, with arrows moving `current`, clamped, and bringing the cell into view, and Enter opening and committing the editor. It also requires CRUD's `crud-list` keys to move the selection. The probe must leave these SC 2.1.1 / 2.4.3 behaviours on the stand tasks it runs unchanged.
- a11y-plan §1 A11y Scope Summary sets tier 0 (SC 2.1.1 · 1.4.3 · 2.4.3). The probe's test or example code brings no new criterion into scope.

- `DioxusDocument::unkeyed_actionable` reads the listener mark `data-dioxus-id`, focusability from `Node::is_focussable()` and the role from `accessibility_tree`. This is the existing bridge-held read of "carries a listener" that link (2) can name (per a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support, sr-actionable-keys; packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/actionable.rs).
- `stand_non_lean_tasks::elements_that_react_to_a_click_and_state_no_role_are_counted` pins the count of elements that react to input but state no role (Cells 677, Circle Drawer 1, the lean tasks 0). It is a measured baseline for a listener-map reading (per a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support, sr-actionable-keys).
- The test harness's `press` / `press_with` drive keys headlessly, and the focused-node query reads them back. This is the route for running a key handler that writes a signal on the stand (per a11y-plan §3 A11y Assertion Harness Contract, keyboard test harness; packages/blitz-test-harness/src/inspect.rs).
- Checks run in both layout modes, and each reads the tree the shell hands the adapter, which equals the harness's tree (per a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support, sr-author-id).

- Never add a second role or name mapping: the snapshot and every reader take role, name and focus from `accessibility_tree` alone (per a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support, sr-snapshot).
- Never surface a control's typed or held value where the plan masks it, for example a password `MASKED_VALUE`. A probe reading signal values must print or field none of them (per a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support, sr-snapshot).

- a11y §7's "reacts to a click" residual ↔ the driver snapshot's `NODE_FIELDS`: the probe's link (2) answer for `click` is the reading that residual waits on, and no field is added here.
- a11y §5's MountedData hazard ↔ the engine-change rule and founder fork (`events.rs`, `dioxus_document.rs` `poll`): Cells' keyboard scroll depends on the hazard staying avoided until he decides.
- a11y §9's `a11y` leg ↔ tests §10's `stand-repeat` leg: `stand_keyboard` and `stand_accessibility_ids` stay in both legs, and a probe check in `tests/blitz-tests/` joins neither unless the plan says so.
- a11y §3's obs log allowlist ↔ obs §6: the probe logs no component name, handler or value, consistent with the redaction of `escher_*` fields.

- `stand_keyboard` still passes in both layout modes after the probe: the Cells walk (`CELLS_TAB_ORDER`, arrows bringing the cell into view, Enter commits) and the CRUD list keys (per a11y-plan §5 Keyboard Navigation).
- `unkeyed_actionable` still returns nothing on every stand task, and the stated reacts-without-role count is unchanged (per a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support).
- The snapshot's `NODE_FIELDS` stays thirteen, with no field saying an element reacts to a click (per a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support).
- The `a11y` CI leg's fourteen files stay green (per a11y-plan §9 CI Integration).

body:
Builds a probe of the four links of the UI graph (node to component, node to handlers, handler to state written, state to reading nodes), each read through what the Dioxus 0.7.3 runtime and escher's dioxus-native-dom bridge already expose, with no fork-level change.
Each link gets one of three verdicts (exposed, exposed with a cost, not exposed without a fork-level change), measured by runs on the headless seven_guis stand (a lean task such as Counter or CRUD plus one served task), in both layout modes where layout touches the reading.
Answers the deferred "reacts to a click" reading: whether a node's click listener is readable from the listener map today.
Re-verifies at HEAD, after the 2026-11-01 upstream sync, the MountedData hazard's mechanism and coordinates (render_immediate holding the document RefCell in poll, the panic at events.rs:162), re-reading the engine-debts reading.
Writes one plain-words reading for the founder: each verdict with its evidence, the cost class of building the UI graph, and the forks needing his word, the MountedData fix among them with its options, not decided here.

body_fields.what: the MountedData hazard's mechanism, `poll` first polling a spawned task inside `render_immediate` while the document's RefCell is held, re-verified at HEAD
the MountedData `RefCell already borrowed` panic coordinate `events.rs:162`, re-verified at HEAD
§A hazard measured beside step 15, the headless measurement through the harness's `poll(None)`

body: The Dioxus DOM bridge in dioxus-native-dom: `DioxusDocument`, DOM events reaching the vdom through `data-dioxus-id`, and `element_id` / `element_ids` with their four tiers (author key, anchored path, component path, document path); the probe reads these for link (1) and link (2) and writes nothing to DOM or vdom.
The bridge's listener reads (the listener map and its event names) as link (2)'s surface, including whether a `click` listener is readable today.
The Dioxus 0.7.3 runtime crates in the dependency graph, read only: components, handlers, signals and their readers are probed through public or bridge-held APIs, each API named in its verdict.
Dioxus stays pinned at "0.7.3": no patch, vendored copy or pin move of any Dioxus crate (the Inherited Defaults and Upstream sync lines that hold Dioxus 0.8.0-alpha.3 back for the next version).

The headless stand `seven_guis::stand`: the four lean tasks with a handler writing state another node reads (Counter, CRUD), its pinned 800x600 Light viewport with one bundled font, offline boots, no telemetry and no env read.
The six served stand tasks behind `escher-session` and the driver `Session` as the home of the served task the probe runs beside a lean one; the probe adds no verb, argument, cause or exit to them.
The test harness (`Harness`): pumping input and `poll(None)` without settling, the shared `VirtualClock` that only `tick` and `advance_time` move; the hazard was measured through its `poll(None)`.
Both layout modes producing identical layouts: a verdict whose reading layout touches is run in both modes.

The MountedData hazard: a task spawned from a key handler that writes a signal is first polled inside `render_immediate`, and a `MountedData` call in it panics `RefCell already borrowed`; named in the reading with its measured mechanism, the windowed path stated as read from the code, not run.
Shell loop and dioxus-native launch path: every window event followed by a Poll, the windowed shell running the same `poll` lines; read, not run, unless a reading needs it.

The rule on direct engine changes for every document (Established Decisions): a MountedData fix is one, so the chunk makes none; the fix is brought to the founder as a fork with its options, and where a chosen fix lands is part of that fork.
Event processing: Dioxus skips event kinds with zero handlers, and handlers run before the default action; this bears on what the listener map shows for links (2) and (3).
Service wiring: shared state is `Rc<RefCell<…>>` and Dioxus services are root contexts; this bears on the RefCell borrow the hazard trips and on what state link (3) and link (4) can read.

Nothing crosses: the driver session's schema (twelve verbs, eight closed causes, the `v3` wire, `command` and `tool_call` spans) and the snapshot, its text and diff stay as they are; no node key, result field, session error, carrier or `NodeId` is added.

Logging: no component name, handler or signal value the probe reads is printed, logged or put in a field; escher-telemetry's field rules (`SAFE_FIELDS`, `CONTENT_FIELDS` redacted) and the ban on a log carrying the snapshot hold over any probe output.
Occupied resources: the probe adds no listener, port, env var, workspace crate, binary name or state directory.
The `accessibility` feature, which gates the dioxus-native-dom snapshot modules, where a probe check reads the snapshot read-only.
The CI gates any probe test or example code must pass: the `test` leg, `stand-repeat`'s zero-failure budget, the clippy, fmt and rustdoc gates, and the per-crate coverage floors.

body_fields.convention: each new integration test file covers one behavior, opens with a `//!` doc naming it, runs its scenario in both layout modes, first asserts the fixture produces the condition, and is one test target per file in blitz-tests

stand checks share helpers through modules under `tests/` that are no test target; `tests/blitz-tests/tests/fixtures/mod.rs` states the fixture boot and hold once, and a page with one reader stays in its check's file
new code passes `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --locked -- -D warnings`, with `clippy::expect_used` / `clippy::unwrap_used` only next to a justification
new modules and files open with `//!` docs, public items carry `///`, and an example opens with a `//!` comment describing what it demonstrates

a Dioxus example declares `#[component]` components with signal and store hooks, reactive state through `#[derive(Store)]`, its CSS in `const` raw strings, and fails with `.unwrap()`, `.expect(..)` or `panic!`
`unsafe` blocks carry `// SAFETY:` comments, and borrow conflicts are worked around by taking a child list or layout out and restoring it

body: The select model and the open select list (`apply_select_choice`, `open_select`, `select_list_view`, `reconcile_select_list`, the select popup's merge surface): the probe reads no select.
JavaScript on Boa (blitz-vibey-script, `ScriptDocument`, the JS bootstrap, timers and module loader): the probe reads a Dioxus app, not page scripts.
The WPT runner, its outputs, bucketing and the WPT and post-results workflows.
The browser app and rdme: history store, navigation provider, document loader, about pages, URL suggester.
Painting and renderer backends: `paint_scene`, layer caps, password masking in paint, vello and skia choices, screenshot rendering.
Networking crates and outbound hosts: blitz-net's provider, user agent, per-host semaphore, HTTP cache, and the hosts list.
Deployment and packaging: publish-browser bundles, the Nix flake, Cross.toml and cross-compilation, signed builds.
Release versioning, build profiles and the MSRV build job.
CSS and layout decisions: CSS approximations, unsupported features, fonts, inline SVG, tables as grid, HTML parsing.
The upstream sync merge surfaces of earlier engine changes (the eight upstreamable changes, `hit_inner`'s conflict with `0980cce5f`, the key-press panic fix): the probe merges nothing.
Style threading and `PARALLEL_TRAVERSAL_LOCK`: the headless stand sets no `style_threading`.
The accessibility adapter `accesskit_xplat` and its platform adapters.
Licensing exceptions and the fixture forms of the google and graphite pages.
Scrolling, hit testing and `visible_region` contracts: no link of the UI graph reads geometry.

body_fields.why: Any probe that reads nodes from the changed set or from a mapping, for example for link (4), must resolve each id through `get_node` and never by indexing.

body_fields.why: Link (4), state to the nodes that read it, must not be read off the changed set as if it were the diff: the contract keeps the two apart and accepts a set flag next to an empty diff.

body: **2026-10-06-stable-element-ids** — registered `DioxusDocument::element_id` / `element_ids` on the bridge, computed on demand from a vdom walk joined with a DOM walk, written to neither DOM nor vdom, and the component-path tier whose segment is the last `::` segment of `VComponent.name` with generics stripped (the four framework scopes adding none, a 2nd+ same-name instance `{name}:{k}`); no `NodeId`, `ElementId`, `ScopeId` or pointer in an id. Recorded as BUILT after dioxus-core 0.7.10 disproved three plan assumptions (base scope `root`, a bare `VComponent.name`, collision-free grammar). Matters here: link (1)'s «exposed» verdict weighs this existing walk as its named API, and the correction is a precedent to measure Dioxus' scope/name shapes rather than assume them.

**2026-10-06-id-stability-across-code-edits** — added the anchored tier (`{key}//{segment}`, inside one component only) and `DioxusDocument::unkeyed_actionable()`, whose readers include `data-dioxus-id`; trap: `UnkeyedActionable.node` is a process-local `NodeId`, so a first wire form must not carry it. Matters here: the four tiers link (1) reads, a listener-mark reader link (2) may name, and the no-`NodeId` rule any probe output keeps.

**2026-10-06-id-persistence** — proved ids persist across re-render, remount and restart in both layout modes; the CRUD row's Dioxus key became the person's `u64`; trap: the html/head/body/#main skeleton built outside the VirtualDom is never remounted. Matters here: a link (1)/(4) reading across a CRUD re-render rests on these persistence facts and must not assume every node is fresh after a remount.

**2026-10-13-upstream-sync-polish-and-ship** (the bridge drops a removed node) — was «`node_id_mapping` entries intentionally not cleared on removal so dioxus-core can reuse detached nodes»; now upstream #1185 drops a removed node with its descendants and clears `element_id_mapping` / `node_id_mapping`, so it reads no id and `get_node` is `None`; the falsy clear became upstream's 28-name `is_bool_attr`. Matters here: links (1) and (4) must be run across a CRUD delete and state what a removed node resolves to through these mappings.

**2026-10-31-engine-debts** (the MountedData hazard of a spawned task) — new Dioxus-integration record, no engine change: a task spawned from a key handler that writes a signal is first polled inside `render_immediate`, holding the document's `RefCell`, and a `MountedData` call in it panics at `events.rs:162`; measured through the harness's `poll(None)`, the windowed path read and not run; Cells' async handles were tried, panicked and did not ship. Matters here: this is the CARRY the chunk folds; P3 re-verifies exactly this mechanism and coordinate at HEAD and the reading names it.

**2026-10-31-engine-debts** (the eight engine changes; Cells' grid) — eight more ratified direct engine changes for every document, each flagged upstreamable, nothing sent, merge surface a line owned by an upstream-sync entry; and `cells-grid` with `onkeydown` calling `MountedData::scroll_to` synchronously, the count of elements that react to input and state no role moving 676 → 677 (every element with the listener mark reading `GenericContainer`). Matters here: the class the MountedData fork's options must state, and Cells as the served contrast to the spawned-task path; link (2)'s listener reading must agree with or explain the pinned 677.

**2026-11-01-upstream-sync-ui-graph** (the key-press panic's fix) — `BaseDocument::deallocate_anonymous_block` clearing stale `layout_parent`s stands beside the eight as a direct engine change for every document, ratified on the founder's F1 A, flagged upstreamable, merge surface owned by «Upstream sync ahead of determinism and exploration»; standing trap: a probe of a panic can read green because its input never reaches the path, so assert the fixture first. Matters here: the precedent the MountedData fix's fork follows, and the trap binds P3's re-measurement of the hazard.

**2026-11-01-upstream-sync-ui-graph** (the queued `mounted` event's guard; citations re-pointed) — `flush_queued_mounted_events` skips an element removed since queued, reading it through `try_element_to_node_id`; upstream's test `element_removed_before_its_mounted_event_is_flushed` left out because it reads 1 mounted event on Dioxus 0.7 where it asserts 0, returned with `286874cc1` through a CARRY; `dioxus_document.rs` citations moved +4. Matters here: the mounted flush after each `poll` is on the hazard's path, Dioxus 0.7 vs 0.8 mounted behaviour differs, and the hazard's coordinates must be re-read at HEAD after this sync.

**2026-11-01-upstream-sync-ui-graph** (merge surfaces' owner; the upstream line at `e42ee1f25`) — the merge surfaces' owner moved to «Upstream sync ahead of determinism and exploration», each flagged upstreamable, nothing sent; upstream read at `e42ee1f25`, merge base unmoved, Dioxus "0.7.3" with no git dependency. Matters here: names the residuals owner a MountedData fix's merge surface would join, and restates the pin the chunk must not move.

- Nothing new lands in occupied resources — no env var, listener, port, workspace crate or binary name (per architecture §Occupied Resources → Environment variables; per architecture §Occupied Resources → Network ports and listeners; per architecture §Occupied Resources → Names).

- The harness pumps and never settles, holds one shared `VirtualClock` moved only by `tick` / `advance_time`, and `settle` never waits on a load (per architecture §Standard Contracts → Test harness); a headless probe drives the stand through it.
- Mutations go through `DocumentMutator`, which flushes deferred work on `Drop` (per architecture §Conventions → DOM API patterns); a probe that writes state does so through the app's handlers, not by mutating the DOM directly.
- Stand apps hold reactive state with `#[derive(Store)]` and signal and store hooks under `#[component]` components (per architecture §Conventions → Apps and examples); links (3) and (4) are read against those hooks.

- No fork-level change: no Dioxus crate edit or pin move and no engine change for every document landed by the probe (per architecture §Inherited Defaults; per architecture §Established Decisions).
- No log, event or field carries a snapshot, an id, a name or a value the probe reads (per architecture §Standard Contracts → Dioxus DOM bridge, its no-log line; per architecture §Cross-cutting Patterns → Logging and timing).
- No raw indexing of `NodeTree` by an id; read ids through `get_node`, since stale-id indexing panics (per architecture §Standard Contracts → Document core; per architecture §Standard Contracts → Scrolling, selection, tree).

- arch ↔ tests: a probe check lives in `tests/blitz-tests/`, one test target per file opening with a `//!` doc and run in both layout modes, its fixture first asserting the condition (per architecture §Conventions → Tests); the harness contract binds the probe's runs.
- arch ↔ obs: the probe adds no span or log field, and the stand installs no telemetry (per architecture §Standard Contracts → Telemetry bootstrap; per architecture §Standard Contracts → Headless stand).
- arch ↔ security: values the probe reads stay masked and never cross; the driver session's no-`NodeId`, no-value rule stays as it is (per architecture §Standard Contracts → Driver session).
- arch ↔ all domains: the work stays in the locked crate names `dioxus-native-dom`, `seven_guis` and `blitz-tests` (per architecture §Existing Scopes).

- `Cargo.toml` still pins Dioxus "0.7.3", and the chunk's diff touches no Dioxus crate source, patch section or vendored copy (per architecture §Inherited Defaults).
- The chunk's diff adds no env var read, listener, workspace crate or binary (per architecture §Occupied Resources → Names).

body_fields.why: the probe must leave escher-session's agent-read output exactly as it is — one JSON line on stdout, fixed stderr lines, the four exit classes, no colour or ESC byte — printing no component name, handler or signal value it reads there, since the scope's «nothing crosses» bound forbids any new exit, verb, field or log line.
body_fields.quote: `escher-session`, the driver's command line (since 2026-10-10-driver-cli), is a surface an agent reads, not a person: a command prints one line of JSON on stdout — the answer, the refusal or a session error's object, keyed by the driver schema's own words — and nothing else there; a usage error prints one fixed line on stderr with stdout empty, and a session error its fixed message on stderr; it uses no colour and no colour dependency, writes no ESC byte on any answer line, and no code asks whether a stream is a terminal, so its output is the same piped or not; the exit status carries the class — `0` accepted · `1` refused · `2` usage · `3` session error

`escher-session`, the driver's command line, and its `mcp` role are surfaces an agent reads, not a person: stdout holds only JSON — one line per command (the answer, the refusal or a session error's object), or newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 lines — never colour or an ESC byte, and no code tests for a terminal, so the output is the same piped or not; the command line's exit status carries the class (`0` accepted · `1` refused · `2` usage · `3` session error), and an `mcp` `Err` ending exits `3`.

**Toolkit / Framework:** winit windows (packages/blitz-shell/src/window.rs:201-207); HTML launches into a native window with `WindowConfig` and the Vello window renderer (packages/blitz/src/lib.rs:106-137; examples/inner_html.rs:28-30; examples/preact_script.rs:37); Dioxus apps open through `dioxus_native::launch` (examples/box_shadow.rs:4; examples/custom_widget.rs:18; examples/counter/src/main.rs:15-17; examples/seven_guis/src/main.rs:4-10; examples/todomvc/src/main.rs:15-19), built from `WindowAttributes` and titled from dioxus-cli-config or "Dioxus App" (packages/dioxus-native/src/config.rs:17-20; packages/dioxus-native/src/lib.rs:238-239)

body:
Builds a probe of the four links of the UI graph (node to component, node to handlers, handler to state, state to readers) through what Dioxus 0.7.3 and the escher bridge dioxus-native-dom already expose, with no fork-level change.
Each link gets a verdict (exposed, exposed with a cost, not exposed without a fork-level change), measured by runs on the seven_guis stand (Counter or CRUD plus a served task), headless, in both layout modes where layout touches the reading.
Answers whether a node's click listener can be read from the listener map today, as link 2's answer for click.
Re-verifies the MountedData hazard's mechanism and coordinates (events.rs:162, poll in dioxus_document.rs) at HEAD, then brings its fix to the founder as a fork with options, without deciding it.
Writes one plain-words reading for the founder (verdicts, evidence, cost class, forks) before the UI graph is planned. The probe code is test or example code only.

body_fields.what: the poll path where render_immediate holds the document RefCell, the mechanism of the MountedData hazard, re-verified at HEAD
the RefCell already borrowed panic coordinate events.rs:162, re-verified at HEAD
the section on the hazard measured beside step 15, the carry's measured mechanism, read back

body: The Dioxus launch path of the desktop-native surface (dioxus_native::launch, as examples/seven_guis/src/main.rs uses it): the seven_guis stand is where the probe runs, through its Counter or CRUD task and a served task.
The bridge DioxusDocument in dioxus-native-dom: its element-id reads and its listener map (event names per node), which links 1 and 2 are read through.
Link 2 for click: whether a node's click listener can be read from the listener map today (the deferred reacts-to-a-click reading).
Links 3 and 4 in the Dioxus 0.7.3 runtime crates (read only): which signal a handler writes, and which nodes or components read that signal.

The MountedData hazard: a task spawned from a key handler that writes a signal is first polled inside render_immediate, and a MountedData call in it panics RefCell already borrowed at events.rs:162. The probe re-verifies this mechanism at HEAD and does not fix it.

The headless test harness the probe measures through: its poll(None), which measured the panic, and its VirtualClock with settle, advance, click and press, which step handlers and spawned tasks without moving the clock unless advance moves it.
The two layout modes, where layout touches a link's reading: each verdict is measured in both.
The windowed shell path (winit window, Vello window renderer) runs the same poll lines. It is read, not run, unless a reading needs it, and the reading says it was read from the code.

The no-fork-level-change bound: no patch, vendored copy or pin move of a Dioxus crate (Dioxus stays 0.7.3) and no engine change for every document. A link that would need one stops at the verdict not exposed without a fork-level change.

Nothing crosses: the probe adds no driver verb, argument, node key, result field, cause, session error, exit, listener, env var, workspace crate, log field or span. The escher-session stdout and mcp output stay as they are, and no component name, handler or signal value the probe reads is printed or logged.

The founder's reading: one document with each link's verdict and its evidence (measured, or marked read-from-code), the cost class of building the UI graph on what is exposed, and the MountedData fix brought as a fork with its options.

body_fields.convention: a probe check added to the blitz-tests crate builds blitz-dom with the system-fonts feature, so text does not measure 0x0 and layout-dependent assertions do not pass vacuously
body_fields.home: the Typography section of the body, under Loading

body: The colour palette: core, surface, text, semantic and border colours, and the SelectListView engine colour constants. The probe paints and styles nothing.
The spacing values and engine spacing: the probe reads components, handlers and state, not spacing.
The depth strategy: observed elevation values, engine depth behaviour and the hit-testing clip rule. The probe does not read or change shadows or hit-testing.
The border-radius values and engine radius handling.
Iconography: the browser toolbar SVG icons, IconButton, the icon size grid, cursors and favicons.
Programmatic scroll-into-view and the driver's scroll behaviour, from the motion section. The probe does no scrolling.
The desktop-native tokens and its titlebar, devtools-overlay and custom-widget component patterns, plus the publish packaging (NSIS, dmg, AppImage).
The mobile-native surface: Android APK, the iOS build, the urlbar, the back button and capture.
The web-spa surface: WASM canvas pages, todomvc's canvas, and bundled WASM font contexts.
The CLI binaries' terminal output colours (owo-colors in the WPT runner, paint_bench and screenshot examples).

The project-wide token sets, type scale, spacing scale, elevation scale and radius scale marked not yet measured, and the sections with no recorded intent (brand identity, anti-patterns, self-validation, design decisions log).

body:
Builds a probe of the four links of the UI graph (node to component, node to handlers, handler to state written, state to nodes reading it), each read through what Dioxus 0.7.3 and escher's bridge dioxus-native-dom already expose, with no Dioxus fork and no engine change for every document.
Each link gets one of three verdicts (exposed, exposed with a cost, not exposed without a fork-level change), measured by a run on the headless stand (a lean task with handler-written state, Counter or CRUD, plus one served task) in both layout modes where layout matters; the probe is test or example code that measures.
Answers whether a node's click listener can be read from the listener map today, as link 2's answer for click.
Re-verifies at HEAD the MountedData hazard: a task spawned from a key handler, first polled inside render_immediate in dioxus_document.rs poll, panics RefCell already borrowed at events.rs:162. It names the hazard and brings its fix to the founder as a fork with options, not decided here.
Writes one plain-words reading for the founder, with each verdict, its evidence and the cost class, before The UI graph is planned; it adds no verb, field, span, log field, listener, env var or crate.

body: The new probe check under tests/blitz-tests: it must install no subscriber, read no env var, print nothing and bind no listener. Its readings go into assertions only, and the silence census reads 0 over its file.

Values masked, never logged: nothing the probe reads (a component name, a handler or event name, a signal's value, node text) is printed, logged, put in a log field or span field, or shown through a Debug print. This is the PII scrubbing rule, applied to the probe's own code.

The headless stand seven_guis::stand (boot, and boot_cells or boot_load for the served task) installs no escher sink. A probe booting it in process has no sink, so a verdict's evidence comes from assertions and never from captured log lines.

Engine features by invocation: a workspace build turns blitz-dom/tracing on, and cargo test -p blitz-tests leaves it off. The probe must give the same verdicts under both builds and must not depend on engine tracing events, which dioxus-native-dom's mutation_writer debug logs fill with text-node contents and attribute values.

dioxus-native-dom as a read surface (DioxusDocument, its element-id and listener reads, poll, events.rs): the probe reads them as they are and adds no log site, tracing call, span or field there. The crate's optional tracing and log-times features stay as they are.

escher-driver's spans stay untouched: the command span with its eight fields and the tool_call span with tool and ending. The probe adds no span or field, so escher-driver keeps its 2 info_span! sites and stand_act_spans its eight fields.

The MountedData panic as error capture: in a binary that installs escher's sink (seven_guis_native, escher-session), the chaining panic hook logs one ERROR event at escher_telemetry::panic with panic.payload redacted, and std's default hook still prints the raw message. The reading states the hazard's mechanism without the probe adding any capture, hook or log line.

The windowed shell runs the same poll lines, so the panic is expected there, but this was read from the code and not run. The reading must keep the measured-or-read mark for each claim: a verdict read from the code and not run says so.

The reading for the founder is a document at rest. It names APIs, verdicts, costs and forks, and holds no probed run values (component names, handler names or signal values from a run). It is not a log line, field or print.
host_log and mcp_log still pass under both builds with 0 needles at trace. The probe touches neither the sink nor the driver, so packages/escher-telemetry and packages/escher-driver stay unchanged.

Any probe code kept under examples/seven_guis holds no print, tracing call, escher_telemetry use, env read, socket, listener or blitz_net. The served-stand silence census still reads 0 over stand.rs and the shared modules.

body: **threat-model-summary ↔ authentication-authorization**: the session socket's trust boundary is the whole of its access control. Its owner-only `0700` directory and `0600` socket with no other authentication (security-plan/threat-model-summary fct-ljkdert4) are the only thing deciding who reaches it, since there is no handshake, token or peer check (security-plan/authentication-authorization fct-c3aavvn3). So a probe that adds no listener, port or carrier keeps both unchanged, and any served-task session the probe drives runs inside that same owner-only boundary.

**threat-model-summary ↔ the body (masked values, no NodeId)**: whatever the probe reads through a session answer (an id, a name, a control value) must stay inside the ratified crossing, with a password's or file input's value masked and no `NodeId` crossing (security-plan/threat-model-summary fct-ljkdert4), on the socket and MCP carriers alike (security-plan fct-z5ttw3ol; security-plan fct-dgkl4a64). Nothing the probe reads about the four links (a component name, a handler, a signal's value) may be put in a field of either carrier.

body_fields.why: The probe must add no field, carrier, node key or exit to the driver session socket and let no NodeId cross, because the scope's «nothing crosses» rules over exactly what this boundary carries.
body_fields.quote: which also sets the rule from that day on — a new field of a closed value set inside an already ratified carrier is not a widening and does not come to him, while a field holding authored text, an open value set, a new carrier or a new exit still does (packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs:39-118; packages/escher-driver/src/json.rs:156-162; packages/escher-driver/src/json.rs:115-134 — the states as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-10-snapshot-states/report.md, `differs` at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-12-self-description/report.md); no `NodeId` crosses

Driver session socket (escher-driver) — the widening rule: a new field of a closed value set inside an already ratified carrier is not a boundary widening, while a field holding authored text, an open value set, a new carrier or a new exit still is.

Driver session socket (escher-driver) — one request line per connection, parsed against a closed grammar under a size bound; anything else is refused with nothing run, and a decoded call runs through `Session::run` alone; one connection at a time under fixed bounds; bounded replies carry ids, names, control values (a password's or file input's masked), snapshot text, diffs, screenshots and a lint's findings, the state readings as closed words and booleans, never an attribute's text, and no `NodeId`.

Markup attributes — the stable element id: the HTML `id` as an author key when non-empty, `/`-free and first in document order, else an anchored, component or document path, so no `id` can make two ids equal; computed on demand and written by escher's code to no log, it leaves by the platform adapter, the driver's answers, MCP results and kept checks, and no `NodeId` crosses.
Markup attributes — a password's or file input's value reads as the fixed `MASKED_VALUE` in the snapshot, its text, diffs and every carrier, never the text, its length or a file's host path

body_fields.why: The probe must add no verb, argument kind, result field or refusal cause to the driver command schema, and any call it makes through a session must go through `validate` inside `Session::run`, because the scope forbids every one of those additions.
body_fields.quote: `validate` checks a call against a closed `'static` table of twelve verbs in three levels

Driver command schema (escher-driver) — `validate` checks every call against a closed `'static` table of twelve verbs and seven bounded argument kinds, returning a typed `Command` or a `Refusal`, the first failure in a fixed order; nothing public runs a `Command` that did not come from `validate`, and the socket, the command line and MCP all pass through it

Driver command schema (escher-driver) — no `unwrap`, `expect` or panic on anything a call supplies, no clock read by the schema or its validation, no `NodeId` kept between calls; one `command` span per call holds fixed words, bools and counts only, never a call's content, the screen text, an image or findings; the crate installs no subscriber and reads no env var.

body_fields.why: If the probe runs its served task through a driver session, the label it passes must be 1 to 32 bytes of `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`, and must never be text read from the document.
body_fields.quote: 1 to 32 bytes of `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`, checked before the caller's boot runs — an invalid label returns `InvalidLabel` with nothing booted; it is never text read from the document, and it is the one caller string a reply carries
Driver session label (escher-driver) — 1 to 32 bytes of `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`, checked before the caller's boot runs; never text read from the document; the one caller string a reply carries.

body_fields.why: The probe must add no exit and no argument, so escher-session's closed argv reader and its four fixed endings stay exactly as they are.
body_fields.quote: four endings — accepted, the answer as one line of JSON on stdout, status 0; refused, the refusal on stdout, status 1; usage, one fixed line on stderr built from the verb table and the app names

CLI arguments (escher-session) — the argv is read by `escher_driver::command_line`, a closed reader with fixed rules; a call is checked by `validate` or `validate_session` before the session address is asked for; four endings with fixed statuses (0 accepted, 1 refused, 2 usage, 3 session error); no ending writes back anything the caller typed, no path on argv panics, and the command line installs no subscriber and reads no environment variable.

body_fields.why: The probe's headless runs query the stand through the harness, whose query helper panics on an invalid selector where the underlying parse returns an error, so each probe query must pass only a valid, fixed selector.
body_fields.quote: Parsed with `parse_author_origin_no_namespace` and parse errors are returned (packages/blitz-dom/src/query_selector.rs:204-210)

body:
Builds a probe, in test or example code only, of the four links of the UI graph (node to component, node to handlers, handler to state it writes, state to the nodes that read it), each read through what Dioxus 0.7.3 and the dioxus-native-dom bridge already expose, with no Dioxus crate change and no engine change for every document.
Each link gets one of three verdicts (exposed, exposed with a cost, not exposed without a fork-level change), measured by runs on the stand: a lean stateful task (Counter or CRUD) and one served task, headless, in both layout modes where layout matters.
Answers the "reacts to a click" reading: is a node's click listener readable from the listener map today.
Re-verifies at HEAD the MountedData hazard: a task spawned from a key handler is first polled inside render_immediate, and a MountedData call panics RefCell already borrowed at events.rs:162. The chunk names it and brings its fix to the founder as a fork with options; it does not make the fix.
Writes one plain-words reading for the founder (each verdict with its evidence, the cost class, the forks) before the UI graph chunk is planned.

body_fields.what: the poll mechanism, the task first polled inside render_immediate while it holds the document's RefCell, re-verified at HEAD
the MountedData RefCell already borrowed panic coordinate events.rs:162, re-verified at HEAD after the upstream sync
the hazard measured beside step 15, the headless measurement of the MountedData panic through the harness's poll(None)

body: The dioxus-native-dom bridge as the probe's read surface: DioxusDocument, its element-id reads (data-dioxus-id, element_to_node_id and try_element_to_node_id in mutation_writer.rs) and its listener map and event names, read only, never changed.

The stable element id the probe reads for node to component: an HTML id author key, else an anchored, component or document path. It is computed on demand and written by escher's code to no log, and no NodeId crosses any carrier.

Nothing crosses: the probe adds no verb, argument, node key, result field, cause, session error, exit, carrier, listener, port, env var, workspace crate, log field or span. So the driver socket's closed grammar, the twelve-verb command schema and the widening rule (a new field, carrier or exit is a boundary widening) stay untouched.

Values masked, never logged: nothing the probe reads (a component name, a handler, a signal's value) is printed, logged or put in a field, in the probe's test output and in the founder's reading alike. A password's or file input's value stays MASKED_VALUE on every carrier the probe touches.

The MountedData hazard's components in events.rs: the MountedData call, try_doc returning None when the document is mutably borrowed, NodeHandle::node panicking with Node does not exist, and MountedError::OperationFailed. The probe measures the hazard's RefCell borrow panic path and does not repair it, because the fix is an engine change for every document, the founder's fork.

The Dioxus nodes panic paths a handler-reading probe can meet: supported event-data conversions unwrap the platform-data downcast, and twelve dioxus event-data conversions reach todo!, unimplemented! or panic!. Link 2's click reading goes through the listener map, never through a conversion that panics.

No fork-level change in the dependency graph: Dioxus stays 0.7.3, with no patch, vendored copy or pin move, and no package enters Cargo.lock. Builds still pass --locked and the cargo-deny audit leg stays green over the resolved graph.

The headless stand harness the probe runs on: the harness's poll(None), settles that never wait on a load in flight, and query helpers that panic on an invalid selector (the probe passes only valid fixed selectors).

If the served task runs through the driver session: the state directory is created 0700 (a group- or other-open one refused), the socket is 0600, the path is a parameter (never an env read or a cwd-relative default), and the label is 1 to 32 bytes of a-z, 0-9 and dash. Every call passes validate inside Session::run.

The probe reads no environment variable beyond the registered test-time ones (CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR, CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR, CARGO_BIN_EXE_escher-session). The escher-driver library and escher-session still read none but RUST_LOG.

escher's own log sink as the probe meets it: escher_telemetry::init's target allowlist redacts engine-target fields and escher content-named fields and drops other targets. The probe adds no log field or span, so the allowlist's lists do not change.
The windowed shell's poll path is read from the code, not run, for the hazard's windowed half. The reading says so, unless a verdict needs a windowed run.

body_fields.convention: each new test reads no env var but the build-time CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR, CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR or CARGO_BIN_EXE ones already registered; a new test-only read is registered as test-only before it lands

each new test that makes a state or recording directory creates it 0700 under the test target directory, with its files 0600 and its path passed as a parameter, and removes only what it created, non-recursively
each new log line or span carries fixed words, bools and counts only, never read content, and passes escher-telemetry's target allowlist with its content-named fields redacted
each new test's or example's dependency is inherited with workspace = true, no package enters Cargo.lock, and every cargo leg still passes --locked under the cargo-deny audit
each committed piece of evidence holds no host path (masked), no typed text, no secret, token or credential-file name, and no kept check beyond the two committed stand-Counter checks
each test diagnostic or debug dump on stdout or stderr holds nothing a caller typed or a document carries beyond the masked values

body: The browser app's at-rest data (the sqlite history store, the HTTP cache on disk, Clear history and Clear Cache, cookies), which the probe neither reads nor writes.

The remote web content boundary and the net provider's per-input checks (file: and data: URLs, fetched stylesheets, iframes, images, favicons, fonts, @font-face, SVG data): the probe fetches nothing remote.
Script execution in blitz-vibey-script (the ScriptFetcher, JS fetch, module imports, script types, JS API argument checks, JS console logging): the probe runs Dioxus apps, not document scripts.

The upstream-only publish-browser workflow, the Signed Builds environment, the macOS and Android signing material, and the wpt-post-results workflow with its trusted-scripts checkout and PR comment splice.
The WPT runner: its local file reads, quarantine and expectation checks, env_logger, WptNetProviderError, and per-test panic catching.
The upstream CLI examples and apps (screenshot, paint_bench, preact_script, multi_doc and its MULTI_DOC env reads, rdme and its comrak unsafe markdown), with their argument parsing and panic paths.
The cold-agent pipe and its agent-written check, the operator's Claude Code login, and the MCP live trial: the probe runs no model session.
Browser navigation surfaces: urlbar parsing, navigation to the external browser, link href resolution, URL fragments, and form submission with its method, enctype and file-path entries.

The engine's layout and paint value guards and panic paths (table roots, unreachable! layout states, degenerate aspect ratios, non-finite geometry, radii and gradient clamps), and the unsafe calc-pointer blocks in stylo_taffy and blitz-dom layout. The probe changes no engine code.
CSS, selector, style element and legacy-attribute parsing, and the markup numeric attributes (rowspan, select size, ol start), which the probe neither changes nor reads as a verdict.
The fixture pages' own requests and subresource integrity (graphite, google, servo, gosub) and the vendored Preact copy.
CI token scoping and the bootstrap phases' records (auth scaffolding, dep-audit tooling install, the logging redaction wire's upstream fmt::init remainder), which this chunk does not change.

body: **2026-10-31-engine-debts** (the `MountedData` panic from a spawned task) — added the error-handling record this chunk re-verifies. A task spawned from a key handler that writes a signal is first polled inside `render_immediate`, which holds the document's `RefCell`, so a `MountedData` call in it panics `RefCell already borrowed`, any app able to meet it. It was measured headlessly through the harness's `poll(None)`; the windowed shell runs the same lines, read and not run. Cells calls its handles synchronously (`drop(handle.scroll_to(…))`, `drop(handle.set_focus(true))`). It was recorded because the planned async form panicked and was not used, and no fix was made. This is the mechanism the founder's reading must restate from a run at HEAD, with its fix left as his fork.

**2026-10-31-engine-debts** (Cells' `cells-grid` keys) — added the Example apps row for the stand's key handler that the hazard's reproduction drives. `cells-grid` takes `tabindex` 0 and an `onkeydown` with a closed key match: arrows move `current`, clamped; Enter opens the editor focused; the editor's Enter commits, stops propagation and returns focus. A click inside a cell's open editor returns early. This was the founder's F13, with the early return on the operator's P2 answer. Probe code on the stand must leave this ratified behaviour holding.

**2026-10-31-engine-debts** (the citations the chunk's edits moved) — re-anchored citations after edits that included `dioxus-native-dom`. It is the origin of the `events.rs` coordinates the hazard record cites, so the chunk must re-check `events.rs:162` at HEAD, not trust the number.

**2026-11-01-upstream-sync-ui-graph** (citations re-pointed to the chunk's tree) — changed 61 lines in their citation digits alone, error-handling.md 2 of them, after the twelve-commit take and the chunk's edits. This is the sync after which the scope asks whether `events.rs:162` and the `dioxus_document.rs` `poll` coordinates still hold: the digits may have moved while the claims did not.

**2026-11-01-upstream-sync-ui-graph** (the mounted event of a removed element) — added an error-handling row: `flush_queued_mounted_events` skips an element removed since its event was queued, through `try_element_to_node_id`, an engine behaviour for every document. The upstream test `element_removed_before_its_mounted_event_is_flushed` is left out: it reads 1 mounted event on Dioxus 0.7 where it asserts 0, and it returns with `286874cc1` (Dioxus 0.8). This is the closest prior change to the mounted-event path. It is a precedent for the option-returning bridge read, and a trap: upstream behaviour that needs Dioxus 0.8 is not reachable at the 0.7.3 pin.

**2026-11-01-upstream-sync-ui-graph** (the key-press panic retired) — fixed a panic that a remote page could reach, which had been recorded and carried and not fixed (2026-10-31-select-popup). The fix is escher's own, on the founder's answer to fork F1 option A: a direct engine change for every document, ratified by his word. Afterwards the operator's reading of the fork was marked as not the founder's own word. This is the precedent for how the MountedData fix must travel: a measured panic carried to the founder as a fork, then fixed only on his answer.

**2026-11-01-upstream-sync-ui-graph** (this take's lock record) — recorded that `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, `deny.toml` and every crate manifest are byte-identical. The pins stay: Stylo "0.22.0", Taffy registry "0.15", Dioxus "0.7.3", winit `=0.31.0-beta.3`, no git dependency. The audit reads `advisories ok`, `licenses ok`. This is the baseline the chunk's acceptance (lock and Dioxus lines unchanged, audit green) is measured against.

**2026-11-01-upstream-sync-ui-graph** (no served port, two test-only TCP binds) — changed the API Security opening from "no TCP or UDP port" to "no served TCP or UDP port". Two `blitz-net` `#[cfg(test)]` loopback binds are registered as test-only, under session rule 2026-10-15. The driver session socket stays the one listener and `mcp` binds nothing. Any listener a probe test opened would owe the same registration; the scope forbids one.

body:
Builds a probe of the UI graph's four links (node to the component that rendered it, node to its handlers and their event names with click as the "reacts to a click" answer, handler to the state it writes, state to the nodes or components that read it), read only through what the Dioxus 0.7.3 runtime and escher's bridge dioxus-native-dom already expose, each link given one verdict: exposed, exposed with a cost, or not exposed without a fork-level change.
Each verdict rests on a run on the headless seven_guis stand (a lean task whose handler writes state another node reads, Counter or CRUD, and one served task beside it), in both layout modes where layout touches the reading; a verdict read from the code and not run says so; the probe's code is test or example code that measures, and what is kept of it is the plan's choice.
Re-verifies at HEAD, after the 2026-11-01 upstream sync, the MountedData hazard's mechanism and coordinates: a task spawned from a key handler that writes a signal is first polled inside render_immediate while the document's RefCell is held in the bridge's poll, and a MountedData call in it panics RefCell already borrowed at events.rs:162, measured headlessly through the harness's poll(None); the windowed path is read, not run.
Writes one plain-words reading for the founder (each link's verdict with its evidence, the cost class of building the UI graph on what is exposed, the forks needing his word) and names the MountedData hazard there with its fix brought as his fork with its options, not decided; no Dioxus crate is patched, vendored or re-pinned and no engine change is made.

body_fields.what: the MountedData panic's coordinate, RefCell already borrowed at events.rs:162, re-verified at HEAD
poll, the render_immediate path holding the document's RefCell when the spawned task is first polled, re-verified at HEAD
the section A hazard measured beside step 15, the headless measurement of the MountedData mechanism read back against HEAD

body: The blitz-test-harness Dioxus-backed construction the probe boots through: Harness::from_vdom, from_component, and the stand's seven_guis::stand::boot(LeanTask, HarnessOptions) for Counter or Crud with stand::options(incremental) as the pinned options, each a fresh VirtualDom rendering the task in TaskShell.
The served task beside the lean one: the stand's boot_cells and boot_load (the load page's options carrying the LoadNet stand-in, every other field kept), the only boots that reach the served pages.

The harness's pump and settle semantics the hazard's reading rests on: pump polls the document with no waker context, resolves at the harness time and is the poll(None) path the panic was measured through; dispatch and dispatch_recorded do not pump; settle repeats the pass, advances no time and logs nothing.

The harness input helpers that drive a handler on the stand: click, press and press_with (the key path the hazard needs, keyboard-types Key, Modifiers and NamedKey re-exported by the harness), type_text, each pumping after dispatch, and the inspection helpers query, node, text_content, attr and dom_string to read which nodes changed.

dispatch_recorded returns the dispatched event names but drives the BaseDocument directly, bypassing Dioxus VirtualDom forwarding: a value bearing on how link (2) and the click reading are measured, since a recorded name is not a Dioxus handler run.

The dioxus-native-dom bridge surfaces the links are read through: DioxusDocument, the stable element id and element_ids(), the listener map and event names, the document's events, and the existing unit-test build of a DioxusDocument from DocumentConfig::default() with initial_build, mark_dirty, poll(None) and a GlobalSignal flipped inside vdom.in_runtime to re-render.

The bridge_tests rule over DioxusEventHandler: its two fields are private to dioxus_document and it has no constructor, so a probe reading a handler from inside the crate sits in a cfg(test) child of that module, and no function under test gains a constructor, a pub or a cfg(test) shim; a reading that needs one is an exposed-with-a-cost verdict to name, not to take.

The unit-level limit of the dioxus-native-dom test helper: DocumentConfig::default() carries the no-op HTML parser, so dangerous_inner_html renders nothing at unit level and parsed markup is read in blitz-tests where the harness has the real parser; a snapshot or layout read at unit level calls resolve(0.0) through inner_mut() first.
Both layout modes: the stand's options take incremental true and false, and a reading layout touches runs in each, as the stand's session and snapshot checks do.
The headless-stand font: the bundled DejaVu Sans with system fonts off and no skip path, so a probe run on the stand measures the same on every runner and in the package-alone build.
Time on the stand comes from the harness's VirtualClock (tick, advance_time, TimerTicks for the Timer): a probe check uses no sleep and no wall-clock read, the session checks' wall-time rule.

Values masked, never logged, over what the probe reads: a component name, a handler or a signal's value is not printed, logged or put in an assertion message or a field; a kept probe check's assertions carry fixed words or a row index only, as escher-driver's command assertions do.

The MountedData hazard as a measured reading: reproducing a known panic in a check (whether by should_panic, catch_unwind or a run read and not kept) is the plan's choice inside the boundary that the fix is not made here and no Dioxus or engine code changes.

A kept probe check in tests/blitz-tests/tests/ joins the agent-run harness's selections (run stand when it carries the stand_ prefix, else run all and run by name) and moves the newest proof reading, run stand 237 over 51 files and run all 733, which a kept target's chunk re-counts.
A kept stand_ file joins the stand-repeat leg and its zero-failure budget (three rounds, no retry), so a probe check kept there must be deterministic on every round in both layout modes.

The engine-features-by-runner rule: the workspace build and the -p blitz-tests build compile the same test file against different engine features (tracing and writing-mode on in the workspace only), so a probe check's green per-package run is not the workspace leg's green.

The coverage leg's per-crate floor on packages/dioxus-native-dom (83 percent, keyboard_compat.rs excluded) still binds if any probe code is kept in that crate; a cfg(test) child file is no record of the per-crate reading.

The stand's process-free reach: the probe runs in process on the headless stand, never through a session host, socket or the windowed seven_guis_native binary, the windowed path being read from the code only.

**Bridge test discipline ↔ the scope's no-fork-level-change boundary**: a probe reading the listener map or the handler through private bridge state does so from a `#[path]` `cfg(test)` child module, adding no `pub`, constructor or shim, which keeps the probe inside the verdict classes and leaves the bridge's surface unchanged (test-plan/test-strategy fct-7m7lxsmy; test-plan fct-i47d76zr).

**Stand fonts and naming ↔ §10 flakiness gate**: a probe check on a stand task asserts under the bundled font with no skip (test-plan/test-strategy fct-2vwamopj), and if it is named `stand_*` it runs in `run stand` and stand-repeat under the zero-failure budget (test-plan fct-temy7g7i); a reading that panics by design stays out of that prefix or is caught inside the check.

body_fields.why: any probe unit test the chunk adds to a crate must sit in an inline `#[cfg(test)]` module, or in a `#[path]` file declared `#[cfg(test)]` at its parent with its test paths unchanged.
body_fields.quote: unit tests sit in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` blocks inside the source file; unit-test modules moved out of line sit in files of their own, each declared `#[cfg(test)]` with `#[path]` at its parent, their test paths unchanged; `dioxus_document::bridge_tests` is a child of `dioxus_document` because `DioxusEventHandler`'s two fields are private to that module and it has no constructor

body_fields.why: a probe unit test of link (2) or (3) that reads `DioxusEventHandler` (the listener map, a handler and the state it writes) must live in the existing `bridge_tests` child of `dioxus_document`, in `dioxus_document_tests.rs`, and not in a new module outside it.
body_fields.quote: `dioxus_document::bridge_tests` in `dioxus_document_tests.rs`, declared `#[cfg(test)] #[path = "dioxus_document_tests.rs"] mod bridge_tests;` at the end of its parent, a child of `dioxus_document` because `DioxusEventHandler`'s two fields are private to that module and it has no constructor (packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document.rs:838-840; packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document_tests.rs:1-6)

body_fields.why: a probe unit test in dioxus-native-dom must build its document the crate's way (`DocumentConfig::default()`, `initial_build`, `mark_dirty`, `poll(None)`, a `GlobalSignal` flipped inside `vdom.in_runtime`). This is the same `poll(None)` path that the MountedData mechanism is re-verified through.
body_fields.quote: the document test builds a `DioxusDocument` with `DocumentConfig::default()`, calls `initial_build`, and drives updates with `mark_dirty` and `poll(None)` (packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document.rs:467-477); the `element_id` unit tests build the same way from a plain `fn() -> Element` app, flip a `GlobalSignal` inside `vdom.in_runtime` to re-render

the bridge tests sit in a `cfg(test)` child module of `dioxus_document` (`bridge_tests`, file `dioxus_document_tests.rs`) because `DioxusEventHandler`'s two fields are private to that module and it has no constructor — they build one over `doc.vdom` and `doc.vdom_state` and call `handle_event` with an `EventState` they keep, the one way to read `propagation_is_stopped()`, a flag nothing else in the workspace reads; no function under test gained a constructor, a `pub` or a `cfg(test)` shim

body_fields.why: a probe check placed in `tests/blitz-tests` must be a new file under `tests/` that auto-discovery picks up, with no `[[test]]` table added and `autotests` not turned off, so that `BlitzTestsTargetsTest` stays green.
body_fields.quote: `BlitzTestsTargetsTest`, one test, reads `tests/blitz-tests/Cargo.toml` with the stdlib `tomllib` and asserts that `[package]` does not set `autotests` to false and that the manifest holds exactly one `[[test]]` table, `all` at `tests/all.rs` with `test = false`: the standing check on the fork's two-line difference from upstream's manifest

body_fields.why: a probe assertion must follow the plan's rule that a failing log prints no value. Its message must carry no component name, handler or signal value it reads, only fixed words, rows or indices.
body_fields.quote: command.rs's assertions over a call carry a row index only, so a failing log prints no argument value

body_fields.why: any probe code kept in dioxus-native-dom's source must keep the crate at its 83 % line floor. A probe test held in a `#[path]` child file adds nothing to the crate's reading.
body_fields.quote: `packages/dioxus-native-dom` 83 %, `packages/blitz-test-harness` 90 %; both `cargo llvm-cov` lines exclude dioxus-native-dom's `keyboard_compat.rs`, upstream's temporary keyboard-types bridge, until escher takes upstream's retirement of it; a `#[path]` test-child file is no record of the per-crate reading

body: **bridge test placement ↔ the scope's surfaces and §3 Crate-local test helpers**: the scope's bridge surface (`DioxusDocument`, its listener reads, `dioxus_document.rs`'s `poll`, `events.rs`) is tested in unit tests only through the `bridge_tests` child. §4 sets the module's place (test-plan/unit-test-strategy fct-dssptnyw) (test-plan fct-tkvntwtm), and §3 sets how it builds the handler and the document (test-plan fct-i47d76zr).

**no constructor, `pub` or `cfg(test)` shim ↔ the scope's verdict classes**: an «exposed» verdict must be measured through the API as it stands, with no constructor, `pub` or shim added to make it readable. A reading that needs one is an «exposed with a cost» verdict that names that change, and the probe's tests do not land it (test-plan fct-i47d76zr).

**assertion messages ↔ the scope's «nothing crosses» boundary**: the scope says nothing a probe reads is printed, logged or put in a field. §4's row-index-only assertion rule is how a probe check keeps that rule even when it fails (test-plan fct-mnyw2bw5).

**blitz-tests target ↔ the CI scripts leg**: a probe target in `tests/blitz-tests` is discovered by file and must leave the manifest's one `all` table untouched. `BlitzTestsTargetsTest` runs in the `ci-scripts` leg (test-plan/unit-test-strategy fct-l2ouwaqy).
**kept probe code ↔ §10 Quality Gates**: whatever the plan keeps of the probe in `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src` is counted against that crate's floor in the `coverage` leg (test-plan fct-4t3fuckc).

This is the boot and font rule every probe run on the stand rests on.

**2026-10-06-stand-test-contract** (the agent-run 5-command contract) — set the `agent-run.sh` selections (`stand` · `all` · `{name}` matching `^[a-z0-9_]+$` with an existing file), the exit grammar and the `run.end` event. A kept probe check is reached only through these selections, and `run stand` only with the `stand_` prefix.

**2026-10-06-stable-element-ids** (element_id unit tests) — recorded the `element_id` unit-test helper: build a `DioxusDocument` from a plain app and re-render through a `GlobalSignal` flipped in `vdom.in_runtime`. Added `stand_element_ids`, one stable id per element in both layout modes. This is the template for a bridge-level probe of link (1) and of a signal-driven re-render.

**2026-10-06-id-persistence** — the stand keeps the same id across a re-render, a remount (fresh `NodeId`s except the four document-skeleton elements) and a fresh process. Link (1)'s node→component reading must go through the stable id, never a `NodeId` that a remount refreshes.

**2026-10-06-snapshot-model** (dioxus-native-dom unit tests re-counted) — the `snapshot` unit tests call `resolve(0.0)` through `inner_mut()` after `initial_build`. Standing practice: each count is appended as a dated link and earlier links are kept as history. A unit-level probe that reads layout must resolve first, and a kept probe re-counts the crate in the same way.

**2026-10-06-id-stability-across-code-edits** — added `actionable.rs` (`unkeyed_actionable`, four unit tests) and the anchored-tier element-id tests (thirteen on the id). These are the bridge-held reads that links (1) and (2) must weigh before giving an «exposed» verdict.

**2026-10-06-snapshot-state-fidelity** — recorded that the unit `build` helper carries the no-op HTML parser, so `dangerous_inner_html` renders nothing at unit level and parsed markup is pinned in blitz-tests. Trap: a headless key press is not the same on every platform (the editor's Backspace arm is compiled out on macOS). A key-driven probe, the MountedData path among them, must not rest on a deleting key.

**2026-10-07-change-tracking-and-diff** — added `Snapshot::diff` and `stand_diff`: real steps on the lean tasks in both layout modes, each step held against the file's own reading of the two snapshots. This is the standing ground truth (click on `counter-increment` naming `counter-value`) for the handler→state and state→node verdicts of links (3) and (4).

**2026-10-07-audit-corrections** (bridge tests, the shared stand module) — created the `cfg(test)` child module `dioxus_document::bridge_tests` in `dioxus_document_tests.rs`. It is a child of `dioxus_document` because `DioxusEventHandler`'s two fields are private to that module and it has no constructor. It keeps the `EventState` it passes, the one way to read `propagation_is_stopped()`. Also made `tests/common/mod.rs` the one shared module that is no target. This is the precedent and the constraint for any probe that reads a handler from inside the crate, and it is why no `pub` or shim may be added.

**2026-10-07-settle-detection** — added `settle`: pump's pass repeated, with no clock read, no time advanced and the changed set neither read nor drained. Traps: a tick delivered after an input helper needs a later pass of its own, and the changed set is non-empty on a freshly booted harness, so a check that reads the flag drains first. Both bind a probe that reads which nodes changed (link (4)).

**2026-10-07-command-and-refusal-schema** — set the assertion discipline: every assertion over a call carries a row index only, so a failing log prints no argument value. A kept probe's assertions must not print a component name, a handler or a signal value.

**2026-10-07-act-by-id** — re-exported `Key` and `Modifiers` from the harness. Rules: a driver check's failure message names a layout mode, a task and an index, never an id or what a screen reads, and no deleting key appears in any check but `stand_act_keys`' one. This binds the messages and key choice of a probe's key-handler drive.

**2026-10-07-driver-command-spans** (engine features by runner) — the same check file read green per package and red in the workspace leg. A check that reads a sink's capture counts lines by target, never in total, and a green per-package run is not the workspace leg's green. A probe verdict names its build.

Gave `run all`'s first stated total. A layout-touching probe reading differs by runner.
